claim: *Engineer–agent interaction through Modeling and Alignment.* Engineers communicate intent and knowledge through natural language, specifications, and models; delegated realization returns evidence through review, testing, and analysis. The channels are complementary rather than sequential. Modeling makes selected engineering knowledge available to guide realization, while Alignment provides evidence for evaluating and revising it.
topology: Two parallel channel fans joined by a single implementation hinge; intent descends and evidence returns.
bw_encoding: Black strokes and text; pale gray headers only. Dashed paths retain optional, missing, or forbidden semantics where explicitly labeled. Position, containment, line weight, and written labels carry distinctions without color.
redesign: Native nodes and routed edges preserve the original semantic structure, with print-sized labels and fewer decorative frames.
alt:
Two panels over one shared implementation node. Left panel, Modeling / Communicating:
    the engineer fans out through three parallel channels — natural language, specification, and models —
    which converge on the agent; the agent produces the implementation. Right panel, Alignment /
    Evaluating: the implementation yields a result, which fans out through three parallel channels —
    review, testing, and analysis — that converge back on the engineer. The same engineer appears at both
    upper ends; the single implementation node at the bottom is the hinge between communicating intent
    and evaluating evidence.
